From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Subject: Acme Corp — Renewal & Expansion recap

Hi Sam / Jules —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned going into Q3 renewal discussions.

Summary of what we heard
- Biggest pain: production latency spikes on large batch inference (50–200 requests) where tail latency occasionally exceeds your 300ms SLO.
- Cost pressure on high-volume inference for anonymization and search re-ranking workloads — current spend pegs at higher per-token unit costs.
- Goal: Lock-in predictable capacity for increased Q4 workloads and reduce per-token cost by ~25% while maintaining current quality.

Current usage / signals
- Q2 token volume ~1.2B tokens/month (attached acme-q2-usage.csv).
- Peak concurrent requests: ~220 (observed during batch rerank jobs).

Proposed upsell path
1) Renewal (Q3 start): 12-month renewal for hosted API at current seat + 20% commit to secure renewal pricing.
2) Q4 Dedicated pilot: 2-GPU Dedicated pool for reranking workloads to stabilize latency and reduce cost — can be scoped as a 3-month pilot.
3) Redwood Optimize add-on: batching & quantization recommendations and guardrails (recommended) to reach the 25% unit-cost target.

Next steps (agreed on call)
- I will send a short proposal + usage attachment for your finance/procurement (attached). Target renewal start: 2026-09-01.
- Sam: confirm internal stakeholders for procurement + any legal timing constraints by EOD next week.
- Naomi & Dylan: I’ve looped you in to scope the Dedicated pilot and technical onboarding.

Attachments: acme-q2-usage.csv, redwood-renewal-proposal-ACME-Q3.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>

Subject: Re: Acme Corp — Renewal & Expansion recap

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the conversation. A few clarifying items from our side:

- The latency spikes are most visible on our nightly rerank pipeline (batch size ~150). If the Dedicated pilot can keep p95 < 250ms there’s strong buy-in.
- On cost: our finance team needs a clear comparison (current hosted vs Dedicated pilot expected spend) and an estimate of realized savings after optimizing.
- Procurement timeline: we try to have renewals executed 30 days prior to renewal start. For a 2026-09-01 start, we’d need signed terms by 2026-08-01.

I’ll introduce procurement contact in a follow-up if needed. Otherwise please send the proposal and any numbers we can share internally.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Sam
Sam Patel
Director of ML Platforms, Acme Corp

Thanks Sam — noted on the timelines. Attaching the proposal and the Q2 usage CSV that should help finance.

Quick answers:
- Dedicated pilot sizing: we recommend starting with 2x A100-equivalent GPUs (can be adjusted up/down) scoped for the nightly rerank job. We’ll provide an estimated cost table comparing current hosted spend vs pilot and projected post-optimize spend.
- SLA & procurement: I’ll include a proposed 30-day payment term and a draft renewal quote that your procurement can route.

Action items I’ll own this week:
- Send formal renewal + pilot proposal (PDF attached).
- Provide a simple cost comparison sheet and recommended performance targets (p50/p95) for the pilot.

If it helps I can also schedule a 30-min follow-up with Dylan (SE) and your infra lead to walk through performance tuning and KV cache behavior.

Attachments: redwood-renewal-proposal-ACME-Q3.pdf, acme-q2-usage.csv

Best,
Marissa
